brand.name: Aglet
brand.tagline: Run the shop between the measure and the install

meta.title: Aglet — CRM for custom cabinet and millwork shops
meta.description: Generic CRMs track deals. Construction suites track schedules. Aglet tracks jobs the way a shop runs them: measure, quote, approve, cut, finish, install.

hero.kicker: Built for shops that cut sheets
hero.headline: Every job, from measure to install, in one place
hero.lede: Generic CRMs track deals. Construction suites track schedules. Neither one knows what a cut list is. Aglet runs the part of a millwork shop that actually breaks — the stretch between the measure and the install.
hero.note: No card required · Import your open jobs from CSV on day one

problem.kicker: Why shops outgrow what they have
problem.headline: The job is not a deal, and it is not a construction project
problem.body: A cabinet job has a shape no general tool models. It gets measured, priced off linear feet and sheet yield, approved with drawings, nested, cut, finished, and installed — and every one of those stages can send it backwards. Shops end up running the real work in a spreadsheet and using the CRM as a contact list.

points.title: Quotes live in spreadsheets
points.body: Priced by linear foot and material, rebuilt from scratch every time, and impossible to compare against what the job actually cost.

points.title: Approvals live in email
points.body: The signed-off drawing is in someone's inbox, and so is the change order that made it wrong.

points.title: Capacity lives in someone's head
points.body: Whether you can take the job depends on what is on the CNC in three weeks, and only one person knows.

how.headline: Six stages, the ones your shop already uses

steps.name: Measure
steps.body: Log the site visit, photos and wall dimensions from your phone. The measure becomes the job.

steps.name: Quote
steps.body: Price from linear feet, material and finish. Paste or import a cut list and Aglet prices against it.

steps.name: Approve
steps.body: Send drawings for client sign-off. Approvals and change orders are recorded against the job, not the inbox.

steps.name: Cut
steps.body: Push the approved cut list to the floor. Sheet count and nesting yield tracked per job.

steps.name: Finish
steps.body: Track finish schedule and booth time — the stage that quietly sets your real lead time.

steps.name: Install
steps.body: Schedule the crew, close the punch list, and lock the job so quoted-versus-actual is final.

features.headline: Built around a cut list, not a contact record

items.title: Quote from a cut list
items.body: Import or paste a door schedule and price it by linear foot, species, finish and hardware. Save the build-up as a template for the next kitchen.

items.title: Shop-stage pipeline
items.body: Measure, Quoting, Approved, Cutting, Finishing, Install — with backwards moves tracked, because that is what actually happens.

items.title: Capacity by machine
items.body: See what is on the CNC and in the booth by week, so you can answer "can we take this?" without walking the floor.

items.title: Client approvals and change orders
items.body: Drawings out, sign-off back, every revision timestamped against the job. The change order is attached to the money it moved.

items.title: Sheet and material tracking
items.body: Sheets consumed, nesting yield and remnants per job — so material variance stops being a surprise at year end.

items.title: Margin per job
items.body: Quoted versus actual on material, labour and finish time. The report that tells you which kind of work to stop taking.

items.q: Does this replace Mozaik or Cabinet Vision?
items.a: No. Those design and nest the work; Aglet runs the job around them. Aglet takes the cut list your CAD produces and handles quoting, approvals, scheduling and margin. Keep cutting the way you already do.

items.q: Can I bring my open jobs over?
items.a: Yes — import from CSV, including the half-finished ones. Most shops are running live inside an afternoon.
No. Aglet tracks quoted versus actual per job and exports to QuickBooks. Your bookkeeper keeps their tools.

items.q: Do my installers need a login?
items.a: They get a mobile job view — drawings, measurements, punch list — without a full seat. Field users do not count against your user limit.

items.q: What if we do commercial casework too?
items.a: Same pipeline. Commercial jobs carry longer approval chains and submittal tracking, which is what the Mill tier adds.

cta.headline: Put this week's jobs in it
cta.body: Import your open jobs, run one quote through it, and see whether the pipeline matches how your shop actually works. Thirty days, no card.

footer.blurb: Aglet is job software for custom cabinet and millwork shops — the stretch between the measure and the install.
